title: Movement Study — Patek Back-Page Print
description: Full-bleed editorial slide built on the silent authority of a Vogue back-page watch spread — one photograph, one wordmark, one italic line. Unlike banner templates that stack elements, this one subordinates every typographic choice to the image.
philosophy: This template exists for the brand that has nothing left to prove. It refuses multiple messages, decorative frames, and any typographic element that competes with the photograph for the viewer's eye. The subject — a wristshot, a movement detail, a crown — occupies the upper third as sovereign; the wordmark and a single italic line live quietly in the lower gutter, acknowledging the image rather than explaining it. It is designed for rooms where restraint reads as confidence, not absence.
goodFor: Luxury watch, jewellery, or perfume brand reveal slides
Single-image hero moments within a premium pitch deck
12-word-or-fewer brand tagline or campaign line reveals
Print-to-screen editorial repurposing for Vogue-adjacent clients
avoidFor: Slides requiring charts, tables, or any data visualisation
Mid-market or budget consumer brands where restraint reads as emptiness
author: harness

examples.promptCore: A luxury editorial cover drawn from the visual grammar of a Vogue back-page spread — the photograph does not illustrate the brand, it is the brand. Mood is cool, unhurried, and sovereign: the silence of something that has nothing left to prove. Compositional rhythm is radically spare — one weighted subject commanding the frame, the wordmark and italic line existing as a whisper in the lower gutter rather than an announcement. Avoid decorative framing, secondary imagery, and any typographic gesture that introduces visual competition with the photograph.

examples.layoutNotes: Edge-to-edge bleed on all four sides — the photograph is the canvas, not an object placed within one. The lower gutter, roughly the bottom fifth of the slide height, is the exclusive typographic zone: wordmark anchored left at the gutter's midline, a single italic line set just below it with generous leading between the two. No header band, no decorative rule, no folio or page number anywhere. Hierarchy is enforced entirely through spatial sovereignty — the image commands by occupying everything above; the text acknowledges by occupying almost nothing below.

examples.promptCore: The slide carries the silence of a magazine spread left open on a glass table — photograph sovereign, words a whisper beneath. Composition is vertical-dominant and asymmetrically weighted toward the image mass, the lower gutter functioning as a quiet exhale rather than a typographic zone. Mood is unhurried authority: no element competes for the eye, no surface ornament intrudes on the image's stillness. Avoid competing visual axes, decorative flourish, centered symmetry, or any layout gesture that implies the words matter as much as the photograph.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed photograph bleeds to all four edges and occupies the upper ~68% of the slide height with no crop margin. A lower gutter spanning the remaining height holds all type within a left-anchored column that begins at roughly 6% from the left edge and terminates at ~50% width, leaving the right half of the gutter entirely empty. Wordmark sits at the gutter's baseline; a single italic copy line floats one line-height above it — nothing else. No rules, no frames, no page number, no header band.
